content:
jen: Heads up — SCIM sync from Okta -> Redwood started failing ~10:12 UTC. About 60 users are stuck in \"pending\" and support is getting 400/409 on provisioning. KMS errors in the audit chain too.
sam: Can you paste the raw error lines from the sync job?
jen: Sure, here's an excerpt from the scim-sync worker log:
```
2026-03-19T10:11:58Z scim-sync[worker]: sync_id=abcd1234 user=jdoe@acme.com status=FAILED err=400 Bad Request {\"detail\":\"invalid externalId\",\"scim_response\":\"HTTP 400\"}
2026-03-19T10:12:01Z scim-sync[worker]: attempt=3 err=rpc error: code=PermissionDenied desc=cloudkms.googleapis.com: permissionDenied: cryptoKeyVersions/2: decrypt failed
2026-03-19T10:12:01Z scim-sync[worker]: service_account=redwood-scim@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com key=projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/scim/cryptoKeys/scim-key
```
sam: That looks like KMS decryption failure on the service account used by the sync job.
maria: We rotated that key yesterday around 02:00 UTC as part of the quarterly rotation, but I thought I left the prior version ENABLED for 7 days. I'll check.
alex: I pulled the KMS audit; the KMS response shows permissionDenied for the SCIM service account on the current key version. Could be the IAM binding wasn't reapplied to the new version.
jen: Quick repro I ran locally against prod service: 
```
curl -s -X POST \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/scim+json\" \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/scim/v2/Users \ 
  -d '{\"userName\":\"test.user@acme.com\",\"externalId\":\"okta|00u1abcd2\"}'
# => HTTP 409 {\"detail\":\"externalId conflict\"}
```
sam: Two separate issues visible: 1) KMS decrypt/permissionDenied -> blocks token decrypt and thus sync jobs fail intermittently. 2) Some requests hit 409s because Okta is sending inconsistent externalId values (we saw displayName in a handful of group-provisioned accounts).
maria: Confirmed: KMS key version 3 was set to DISABLED by the rotation script due to a bug in the automation. I still have the previous version (v2) but the key version used by the service principal was v3. I'll re-enable v3 temporarily.
alex: After v3 re-enable, we should confirm the service account has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter for the cryptoKey. Run:
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy scim --keyring=scim --location=global --project=redwood-prod
# then look for bindings with members: serviceAccount:redwood-scim@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
jen: I just re-enabled v3 (thanks @maria) and restarted a single sync job. Initial log shows decrypt succeeded and that particular user's provisioning moved to SUCCESS.
sam: Good. For the 409s we need an Okta mapping fix. In the Okta SCIM app we currently map externalId -> user.profile.nickName for some orgs. That should be user.id. Changing that will avoid collisions.
maria: I'll patch the rotation runbook to ensure new key versions remain ENABLED until all consumers confirm. Also adding an automated IAM verification step after rotation.
alex: For remediation plan: 1) re-enable key version (done), 2) run a dry-run batch for 50 users, 3) update Okta mapping to use user.id, 4) re-run delta to resolve conflicts, 5) create a short maintenance window and notify support.
jen: I'll coordinate the dry-run now and open an incident for tracking.
oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-43: scim-sync-prod-kms-error (severity=P2) — assigned to eng-security.
sam: Also add a quick audit query to surface any other service accounts that lost cryptoKeyDecrypter during rotation. Example BigQuery/GCloud filter: auditLog protoPayload.methodName=google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyService.Encrypt OR Decrypt with status.code=7
jen: Will add that to the ticket. Also noticed ~8 users had externalId duplicates; those will require manual merge in Okta or a patch flow. I'll list them in the ticket.
maria: I'll follow up with ops/infra to fix the rotation automation and add a CI guard.
jen: Thanks all — planning to run the full re-sync in 1h after small-batch verification. I'll post updates in this thread and ping @support to surface to customers. :thumbsup:
